newsitem.title: USA: California city targets companies in Burma.
newsitem.headline: California city targets companies in Burma.

text.p: California's seaside community of Santa Cruz said on Wednesday it would penalize companies that do business in Burma, joining a list of governments to lash out at the military-ruled state.
The Santa Cruz resolution would prohibit city investment in American companies that do business in Burma and make it harder for those companies to win city contracts.
The resolution was unanimously approved by the city council at a late-night meeting on Tuesday.

President Bill Clinton in mid-May officially imposed economic sanctions on Burma. The United States and other Western countries accuse Rangoon of human rights abuses and repression of the democracy movement.
A Massachusetts law imposes a pricing penalty on state procurements from companies that do business in Burma.
Earlier this year, New York City's mayor signed a law barring the city from dealing with companies that do business in Burma.
